onesa_matter.title: Why Onesa AI Matters
onesa_matter.headline: Africa deserves AI that understands Africa.
onesa_matter.p1: Across the world, AI is reshaping economies, industries, and societies at incredible speed. Yet most models are built on data, priorities, and contexts that often miss African realities. For Africa to fully participate in the global digital economy, we need Africa-centric models that understand our languages, cultures, business environments, and development priorities.
onesa_matter.p2: At Diaspora Unlocked, we believe Africa should not only consume AI. Africa must help build it. That belief is exactly why we began developing Onesa AI: to create intelligent systems that are truly relevant to African markets, African data environments, and African economic transformation goals.
onesa_matter.p3: We also know this journey is not easy. Training AI models demands serious infrastructure, computing power, data preparation, and world-class talent. The costs are high, and the barriers are real. We chose to move forward anyway because Africa's long-term future depends on technological ownership, digital independence, and the ability to shape our own digital ecosystems.
onesa_matter.p4: AI sovereignty is becoming one of the defining global conversations of this era. Nations that control their data, their models, and their digital infrastructure will be better positioned to protect their economies, accelerate innovation, and preserve strategic independence. Africa must be in that future, not as observers, but as creators and leaders.
onesa_matter.p5: Onesa AI is our commitment to that future. This is bigger than technology. It is about opportunity, resilience, and building systems that serve future generations across the continent and the diaspora.

export.objective_title: Export to the EU with Confidence
export.objective_subtitle: Zimbabwe exporters can access the EU under iEPA duty-free and quota-free terms. Focus on REX registration, origin documentation, SPS compliance, and current EU regulatory changes.
export.contact_form_subtitle: Fill out the form below to get in touch with our export specialists.
export.market_requirements_subtitle: Core steps required to claim preferential access and clear EU import controls.

requirements: Exports to the EU are governed by the interim EPA (iEPA), giving Zimbabwe duty-free and quota-free market access.
Since July 1, 2021, exporters must use the EU Registered Exporter (REX) self-certification system.
Register as an exporter through ZIMRA to issue valid Statements on Origin under REX.
Consignments above EUR 6,000 require a Statement on Origin from a registered REX exporter.
Consignments at or below EUR 6,000 can be self-certified by any exporter (without REX registration).
Keep origin documentation audit-ready for customs checks in both Zimbabwe and the EU.
Typical ZIMRA registration pack includes application letter, certificate of incorporation, CR6/CR14, and valid ITF263 tax clearance.
Obtain an export license where required by sector ministries (for example Agriculture for plants).
Core shipping file must include commercial invoice (with HS code), packing list, and bill of lading or air waybill.
Food and plant exports must meet strict SPS requirements, including traceability and health controls.
Market trust often depends on certifications such as GLOBALG.A.P. and HACCP.
For honey, compliance work includes a National Residue Monitoring Plan (NRMP) aligned to EU requirements.

export.product_intelligence_subtitle: Stay ahead with real-time data on product demand, pricing, and buyer preferences.

tourism.attractions_subtitle: Iconic landmarks that define the Zimbabwean experience.

vicfalls.name: Victoria Falls
vicfalls.desc: One of the Seven Natural Wonders of the World, the world's largest sheet of falling water
vicfalls.summary: Known locally as Mosi-oa-Tunya (The Smoke That Thunders), Victoria Falls is twice the height of Niagara Falls. Experience white-water rafting, bungee jumping, helicopter flights, and the famous Devil's Pool. The falls are at their most spectacular from February to May during peak flow.
quickFacts: Located on the Zambezi River at the Zimbabwe-Zambia border.
Approximate width is 1.7 km with a drop of over 100 m at its deepest sections.
Protected within the Mosi-oa-Tunya / Victoria Falls World Heritage landscape.
experiences: Scenic viewpoints, rainforest walks, and photography trails.
Adventure options such as rafting, bungee jumping, and helicopter flights.
Nearby safari and river experiences in surrounding protected areas.
vicfalls.bestTime: High-water spectacle is usually strongest from late rainy season into early dry season; lower-water months are often preferred for some adventure activities.

greatzim.name: Great Zimbabwe
greatzim.desc: Ancient stone ruins showcasing medieval African civilization and architectural excellence
greatzim.summary: Built between the 11th and 15th centuries, Great Zimbabwe was the capital of the Kingdom of Zimbabwe. The massive stone structures were built without mortar, showcasing sophisticated engineering. The site gives the country its name and remains a powerful symbol of African achievement.
quickFacts: Constructed and expanded between the 11th and 15th centuries.
Famous for dry-stone masonry built without mortar.
Represents the political and cultural center of the historic Zimbabwe civilization.
experiences: Explore the Hill Complex, Great Enclosure, and Valley Ruins.
Interpretive historical tours and local cultural storytelling.
Panoramic viewpoints over the wider Masvingo landscape.
greatzim.bestTime: Accessible year-round; dry season months are generally better for walking and site exploration.

kariba.name: Kariba Dam
kariba.desc: One of the world's largest man-made lakes, perfect for houseboating and fishing
kariba.summary: Lake Kariba stretches over 5,500 square kilometers along the Zambezi River. Famous for world-class tiger fishing, houseboat holidays, and stunning sunsets. The lake is home to abundant wildlife including hippos, crocodiles, and elephants along its shores. Matusadona National Park offers excellent game viewing.
quickFacts: Sits on the Zambezi corridor and supports both tourism and recreation.
Popular for boat-based travel, fishing tourism, and sunset cruises.
Connected to nearby wildlife areas including Matusadona-facing zones.
experiences: Game-viewing combinations with lake and park circuits.
kariba.bestTime: Dry season is typically preferred for wildlife viewing; lake activities operate across most of the year.

rocks.name: Balancing Rocks
rocks.desc: Iconic natural rock formations that symbolize Zimbabwe's unique geological heritage
rocks.summary: These gravity-defying granite formations appear on Zimbabwe's currency and are found throughout the country, particularly in Matobo National Park. Formed over millions of years through erosion, the rocks create surreal landscapes perfect for photography, rock climbing, and nature walks.
quickFacts: Prominent around Matobo and other granite landscapes.
Featured in national symbolism, including currency imagery.
Formed through weathering and erosion of ancient granite outcrops.
experiences: Landscape photography and short nature walks.
Rock-art and heritage combinations in Matobo areas.
Scenic drives linking Harare and Matobo viewpoints.
rocks.bestTime: Year-round attraction; clear dry-season weather often gives the best visibility for photos.

tourism.other_attractions_subtitle: Beyond the iconic landmarks, Zimbabwe offers diverse landscapes and wildlife experiences across the country.

hwange.name: Hwange National Park
hwange.desc: Zimbabwe's largest park, famous for its massive elephant herds and diverse wildlife.
hwange.summary: Covering over 14,000 square kilometers, Hwange is a premier safari destination. It hosts over 100 mammal species and 400 bird species. The park is world-renowned for its elephant population, numbering in the tens of thousands, and offers some of the best game viewing in Africa.

matobo.name: Matobo National Park
matobo.desc: A UNESCO World Heritage site known for its balancing rocks and spiritual history.
matobo.summary: Matobo Hills features a unique landscape of granite whaleback dwalas and broken kopjes. It is a significant archaeological site with one of the highest concentrations of San rock art in Southern Africa and is the burial place of Cecil John Rhodes at 'World's View'.

eastern_highlands.name: Eastern Highlands
eastern_highlands.desc: A cool, mountainous region offering lush forests, waterfalls, and misty peaks.
eastern_highlands.summary: Stretching along the border with Mozambique, this region includes the Nyanga, Vumba, and Chimanimani mountains. It offers a stark contrast to the rest of the country with its alpine scenery, trout fishing, and the highest point in Zimbabwe, Mount Nyangani.

mana_pools.name: Mana Pools National Park
mana_pools.desc: A remote UNESCO site famous for its river-fed pools and walking safaris.
mana_pools.summary: Located in the Zambezi Valley, Mana Pools is known for its incredible beauty and the four large pools formed by the river. It offers a unique opportunity for unguided walking safaris among elephants, lions, and African wild dogs in a raw, prehistoric landscape.

nyanga.name: Nyanga National Park
nyanga.desc: The 'Little Scotland' of Africa, home to Zimbabwe's highest peak and deepest falls.
nyanga.summary: Nyanga is a highland paradise featuring Mount Nyangani and Mutarazi Falls (Africa's second highest). Visitors enjoy fly-fishing, golfing, and the adrenaline-pumping skywalk and zipline over the deep Pungwe Gorge.

gonarezhou.name: Gonarezhou National Park
gonarezhou.desc: The 'Place of Elephants,' characterized by the stunning red Chilojo Cliffs.
gonarezhou.summary: As Zimbabwe’s second-largest park and part of the Great Limpopo Transfrontier Park, Gonarezhou is famed for its rugged scenery and iconic red sandstone cliffs. It offers a truly wild experience for those looking to get off the beaten track.

regulatory_snapshot.title: Investment Regulation Snapshot
regulatory_snapshot.subtitle: Before investing, verify ownership eligibility, licensing, exchange-control registration, and market-specific limits for foreign participation.
checklist: Check if your target activity is reserved under Statutory Instrument 215 of 2025 before committing capital.
If operating in a reserved sector, plan compliant local equity restructuring timelines and legal documentation.
Apply for a ZIDA investment license through the DIY portal to secure statutory investment protections.
Set up entity structure and appoint a local representative/proxy director for legal notices and operations.
Register qualifying cross-border investments, royalties, and recurring technical fee agreements with RBZ.
Model exchange-rate and settlement exposure across USD and ZiG under the multi-currency framework.
For listed exposure, account for ZSE foreign shareholding limits and assess VFEX USD-based alternatives.
In financial models, include applicable non-resident withholding taxes and export-incentive tax treatment.

product_approval.description: Start with market access and product classification

For restricted product categories, obtain sector-specific approvals first.

Track CBAM developments for carbon-intensive products and contracts.
Prepare commercial invoice, packing list, and bill of lading/air waybill.
Include correct origin declarations and shipping marks.
Align payment terms with exchange-control and banking requirements.
Keep complete records for audits, claims, and repeat shipments.

success.objective_subtitle: Showcasing the tangible impact of diaspora engagement across various sectors and communities in Zimbabwe.

leather_goods.title: Leather Goods Export Success
leather_goods.story: A group of Zimbabwean diaspora professionals in Germany connected local leather manufacturers with European retailers. The diaspora network provided market intelligence on German consumer preferences, direct introductions to retail buyers, quality assurance guidance, and ongoing product development support.
leather_goods.testimonial: The ZIGD platform connected us with diaspora members who understood both our craftsmanship and European market demands. Within 18 months, we went from local sales to exporting to three European countries.
leather_goods.author: Tendai Moyo

horticulture_breakthrough.title: Organic Horticulture Breakthrough
horticulture_breakthrough.story: A small-scale farming cooperative achieved EU organic certification with support from diaspora agronomists. The project now exports high-value vegetables to European supermarkets, with diaspora members providing technical expertise, certification guidance, and buyer connections.
horticulture_breakthrough.testimonial: We never imagined our small farm could meet European standards. The diaspora experts walked us through every step of organic certification and connected us directly with buyers.
horticulture_breakthrough.author: Grace Ncube

tourism_lodge.title: Tourism Lodge Investment
tourism_lodge.story: Through ZIGD's crowdfunding platform, 280 diaspora investors pooled $500K to develop an eco-lodge near Victoria Falls. The lodge now generates steady returns while providing employment and supporting local communities. Diaspora investors receive quarterly dividends and enjoy preferential booking rates.
tourism_lodge.testimonial: I invested $2,000 from the UK and now I'm part-owner of a beautiful lodge in my homeland. The transparency through NTIR gave me confidence, and the returns have exceeded expectations.
tourism_lodge.author: Simba Chikwanha

stone_sculpture.title: Stone Sculpture Export Network
stone_sculpture.story: Zimbabwean sculptors gained access to North American art markets through diaspora gallery owners and art dealers. The network provides market insights, handles logistics, and promotes Zimbabwean art at international exhibitions. Sales have tripled in two years.
stone_sculpture.testimonial: Our sculptures are now displayed in galleries across three continents. The diaspora network understood both our artistic vision and international market dynamics.
stone_sculpture.author: Patrick Mavros

tech_startup.title: Tech Startup Diaspora Funding
tech_startup.story: A Harare-based fintech startup raised $750K from diaspora investors through ZIGD's investment platform. The company developed a mobile payment solution for rural areas, now serving 500K+ users. Diaspora investors provided both capital and technical mentorship.
tech_startup.testimonial: Diaspora funding came with more than money—we gained advisors who understood Silicon Valley standards and African market realities. Their guidance was invaluable.
tech_startup.author: Tafadzwa Chidavaenzi

honey_export.title: Honey Export Cooperative
honey_export.story: Rural beekeepers formed a cooperative to export organic honey to Europe. Diaspora food scientists helped achieve EU certification, while diaspora business professionals secured contracts with specialty food retailers. The cooperative now supports 120 families.
honey_export.testimonial: From selling honey by the roadside to exporting to European supermarkets—the diaspora network made this transformation possible through technical support and market connections.
honey_export.author: Rudo Makoni

heritage_tourism.title: Heritage Tourism Package Success
heritage_tourism.story: A tourism operator developed specialized diaspora homecoming packages through ZIGD's platform. The packages combine family visits with cultural tourism, attracting over 1,200 diaspora tourists annually. The business employs local guides, drivers, and hospitality staff.
heritage_tourism.testimonial: We created experiences that help diaspora reconnect with their roots while supporting local communities. ZIGD's platform gave us visibility to our target market.
heritage_tourism.author: Chipo Mutasa

macadamia_nut.title: Macadamia Nut Processing Plant
macadamia_nut.story: Diaspora crowdfunding enabled construction of Zimbabwe's first macadamia processing plant. The facility processes nuts from 200+ small-scale farmers, adding value before export. Government procurement contracts provide stable demand while export markets drive growth.
macadamia_nut.testimonial: We raised $1.2M from diaspora investors who believed in value-addition. Now we're creating jobs, supporting farmers, and exporting premium products to Asia and Europe.
macadamia_nut.author: Ngoni Sibanda

regulations.title: Regulations & Compliance Guide
regulations.subtitle: Practical regulatory guidance for diaspora investors, exporters, and returnees. Use this as an execution checklist and align final decisions with qualified legal, tax, and sector advisors.

investment_compliance.title: Investment Compliance
points: Confirm project legal structure, ownership, and board controls before funding.
Verify licensing and approvals through ZIDA and relevant sector regulators.
Use written shareholder and governance agreements for diaspora co-investment.
Document source of funds and perform KYC/AML checks on counterparties.

currency_settlement.title: Currency, Repatriation, and Settlement
points: Agree settlement currency (USD/ZiG/other) and payout schedule in contracts.
Define dividend and exit mechanics clearly for diaspora participants.
Use bank-compliant channels with full transaction traceability.
Include FX and transfer-risk provisions in investment term sheets.

export_controls.title: Export Trade Controls
points: Validate HS classification, destination-market restrictions, and permits.
Maintain certificate packs: origin, phytosanitary, and quality documents.
Align labeling, packaging, and traceability to destination-market rules.
Use approved freight and customs brokers for controlled product categories.

export_certification_and_labeling.title: Certification and Labeling
points: Map each product to required standards before buyer onboarding.
Pre-audit facilities and records before external certification runs.
Maintain lot-level traceability for food, wellness, and craft exports.
Run periodic compliance checks to avoid border holds and penalties.

tourism_entry_and_safety.title: Tourism Entry and Safety
points: Check visa category, permitted stay, and document validity before travel.
Carry travel insurance aligned to planned activities and medical needs.
Confirm payment channels and transaction limits in advance.
Follow local park, road, and accommodation compliance requirements.

due_diligence_checklist.title: Diaspora Due-Diligence Checklist
points: Entity verification, UBO checks, and litigation or sanctions screening.
Contract review across commercial, tax, and dispute-resolution clauses.
Operational proof: site inspections, audited financials, and supplier validation.
Ongoing controls: reporting cadence, KPI tracking, and escalation matrix.
